scope: Virtual web page reading, links and headings lists, immediate Ctrl silence and reliable search/confirmation handling.

topics.title: Virtual page view and element lists
details: Web pages render in Companion as a stable, read-only virtual text view with element positions. Arrows read text and announce link, heading and control roles; existing quick keys, forms and table navigation use the same view across Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Brave. Page loading announces the title, site, heading/link counts and first line.

F7 or Insert+F7 opens links; F6 or Insert+F6 opens headings. Say List links or List headings. Up/Down, Home/End and first-letter navigation browse the list. Enter or Open current link opens the chosen link; Enter or Go to heading moves the virtual caret to the selected heading. Escape or Close list returns to the page.

topics.title: Silencing speech and responsive confirmation
details: Ctrl silences Companion independently of microphone wake/sleep state and foreground window. Windows key-state polling runs on the local speech thread and interrupts local, eSpeak and AI speech; delayed caret and phonetic feedback is canceled.

Link lists no longer create a Yes/No prompt for each item. Explicitly opening an ordinary link activates it directly. Guided intent suggestions and potentially consequential buttons retain their review safeguards. Remaining web confirmations expose keyboard Y/N and Enter/Escape even when a list is active; voice confirmation and list commands are accepted during local feedback.

topics.title: Page extraction and search engine choice
details: The virtual view traverses visible content in display:contents and zero-rectangle layout containers, preserves link destinations and labels, and reads each link/control on a virtual line. Large-page key generation avoids a spread argument limit; control lookup uses a map. Hidden verification frames no longer mark an otherwise readable page as blocked.

Search stays on the requested engine. An empty or blocked Brave Search page no longer silently redirects to DuckDuckGo. Readable verification prompts are reported, and another search engine remains a deliberate user choice. Native focus polling does not replace virtual-page or element-list speech.

topics.title: Documentation and verification
details: Built-in Help and versioned What’s New documents describe the virtual view, list shortcuts, direct link activation and Ctrl silence. Regression tests cover all reported paths; Windows live tests exercise all four supported browser adapters with layout-container and list fixtures. Public-site behavior still needs beta testing.
